en.intro: Carry on from the line of kings, and listen to the word Krishna uses to call Arjuna.
en.body: O scorcher of foes, this yoga was known by the royal sages through an unbroken lineage. In the course of great time, this yoga was lost in this world. Arjuna is called Parantapa, scorcher of foes, and with that single name Krishna reminds him of his warrior nature as he speaks of a yoga once passed down by royal sages. Krishna says that because Arjuna is his friend and devotee, this ancient yoga is now being taught to him today.

issues: meaning_changed: "हे अर्जुन, इस तरह यह योग राजर्षियों द्वारा परम्परा से प्राप्त हुआ था।" (The Hindi translation drops the crucial word 'परन्तु' (but/however) from the SOURCE translation ('परन्तु बहुत समय बीत जानेके कारण'), which completely changes the meaning. The Sanskrit and English indicate that the yoga was known by royal sages but was subsequently lost over time, whereas the Hindi translation simply states it was received by royal sages without conveying the loss.)

meaning_changed: "हे अर्जुन, इस तरह यह योग राजर्षियों द्वारा परम्परा से प्राप्त हुआ था।" (The Hindi translation omits the vocative 'परंतप' (O scorcher of foes) and replaces it with 'हे अर्जुन'. The SOURCE and English translation explicitly call Arjuna 'Parantapa', which is the exact point of the notice. The Hindi intro calls the listener to hear what Krishna calls Arjuna, but the actual meaning translation omits the address entirely.)
